introduction_markdown:
**Cameroon General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination / Technical and Vocational Education Examination. Subject: Religious Studies (code 0785), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2020. Paper 2: The Old Testament/Jewish Bible and World Faiths. Duration: three hours.**

Instructions to candidates: Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY. All questions carry equal marks (25 marks each).

You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers.

Sections of the paper: 1.0 The Old Testament/Jewish Bible, Section 1.1 The Patriarchs to David (questions 1 to 6); Section 5.3 Islam (questions 7 to 12); Section 5.5 African Traditional Religious Beliefs and Practices (questions 13 to 18).
incertitudes: Question 7 : points imprimés (a) 5 marks et (b) 20 marks, soit 25. L'énoncé imprime « Al-Qur'an » ; le corrigé écrit « the Qur'an » et « Al-Qur'an » indifféremment.
Neutralité : les croyances sont présentées comme celles des musulmans (« Muslims believe », « according to Islamic tradition ») ; aucun numéro de sourate ni de hadith n'est cité.

Règle de choix : le sujet impose « Answer FOUR questions chosen from any ONE SECTION ONLY ». Cette règle (4 questions d'UNE SEULE section) n'est pas exprimable avec `parmi` (un seul groupe) ni `ou` (sous-questions) : `regles_choix` reste vide dans tous les fichiers et la consigne complète est recopiée dans `introduction_markdown`.

Aucun corrigé officiel : les corrigés sont des réponses modèles rédigées de mémoire, sans accès à une source ; les références sont limitées à des passages et faits bien établis, les autres points sont formulés prudemment (« according to Islamic tradition », « Muslims believe »). À faire relire par un spécialiste des études religieuses avant mise en avant.

questions.corrige_markdown: Al-Qur'an (literally "the recitation" or "the reading") is the holy book of Islam. Muslims believe that it is the word of God (Allah), revealed in Arabic to the Prophet Muhammad through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) over a period of about twenty-three years, beginning in 610 CE in Makkah (Mecca) and ending in Madinah. It is divided into 114 chapters (surahs) of unequal length, which are made up of verses (ayat), and it opens with Surah al-Fatihah. Muslims believe that it contains guidance for belief, worship, morality and law, and that it is the final revelation, confirming earlier scriptures. It is memorised, recited in prayer and written down, and it is the first source of Islamic teaching and law.

questions.enonce_markdown: (b) How unique is the Qur'an in Islam? [20 marks]
questions.corrige_markdown:
**Introduction.** For Muslims the Qur'an holds a place that no other book, and no other source, can have. Its uniqueness is both religious and practical. The points below describe what Muslims believe about it.

**1. Its divine origin.** Muslims believe that the Qur'an is not the composition of Muhammad, who was unlettered, but the speech of God, delivered word for word through Jibril. Unlike other sources of Islam, such as the sayings of the Prophet (hadith), which transmit his words and actions, the Qur'an is considered God's own wording, and its authority is therefore absolute.

**2. Its language.** The Qur'an is in Arabic, and Muslims hold that it should be recited and prayed in Arabic. Translations are regarded as interpretations of the meaning, not as the Qur'an itself. This gives Muslims all over the world a common sacred language.

**3. Its inimitability (i'jaz).** The Qur'an itself challenges its opponents to produce something like it. Muslims regard the beauty, depth and eloquence of its Arabic as a miracle, indeed as the lasting miracle of the Prophet, unlike the miracles of earlier prophets which were bound to their time.

**4. Its preservation.** Muslims believe that God promised to protect the Qur'an from alteration. In practice it was memorised by many companions (the huffaz) and written down during the Prophet's life. It was compiled in book form after his death (under Abu Bakr and standardised under the caliph Uthman), and it has been transmitted with a very high degree of agreement in text. Millions of Muslims today memorise the whole text.

**5. Its place as the primary source of law and guidance.** The Qur'an is the first source of the Shari'ah, followed by the Sunnah, consensus (ijma') and analogy (qiyas). It guides beliefs (the oneness of God, prophets, the Last Day), worship (prayer, fasting, zakat, pilgrimage) and conduct (justice, family life, trade, treatment of the poor, orphans and neighbours).

**6. Its role in worship and daily life.** It is recited in every ritual prayer, in Ramadan (the month in which it began to be revealed), at births, at funerals and at many other occasions. It is treated with reverence: Muslims perform ablution before touching the written text, and keep it in a place of honour. Recitation and calligraphy have become major arts in Muslim cultures.

**7. Its claim to be universal and final.** Muslims believe that the Qur'an confirms the earlier revelations (the Tawrat, the Zabur and the Injil) but corrects the changes introduced, in their view, in the scriptures of earlier communities, and that it is the final message for all humankind. This claim distinguishes how Muslims see it from how other communities see their own scriptures.

**Conclusion.** The Qur'an is unique in Islam because Muslims believe in its divine origin, its Arabic form, its inimitable style, its preservation, its authority as the primary source of law and its constant presence in worship and daily life. It is the foundation on which the Islamic faith and community rest.
